subject: Detached isolated S5 retry reaches dry-bank waypoint 11 and stops before wreck sandbags
scope: One isolated original-client 1.16.5.0 run, ordinary copied Game DLL, archived post-Conrad-corpse character DB, and only copied objective 1995/1 timer anchor reset. This was a diagnostic, not an uninterrupted original-timer route.

exact_locations: focus-second.png captured just before final hold
commands/ timestamped JSON plus matching result files

observations.finding: The detached supervisor PID 3741791 had PPID 1 and SID 3741791. It owned launcher PID 3741792 and driver PID 3741793. Both remained running for the 302.55-second route until the driver exited 1. This confirms the detached process lived across read-only polling and avoided the prior immediate paired exec-session SIGTERM in this attempt; it does not prove the original signal source or universal stability.
observations.source_location: supervisor-events.jsonl; supervisor-state.json; observed ps before terminal

observations.finding: The client traversed the dry-bank route to waypoint 11. From accepted (-167.89062,91.21875,-16.695312), yaw 0.33373672, the next hold toward (-169.727,95.113,-22.375) produced a stationary packet, then accepted (-168.08594,91.40625,-16.875), yaw 0.31178162. Target distance improved only 0.23 m, below the 0.35 m guard within its 8-second window. The driver stopped before the earlier wreck sandbag positions; no south/right clearance probe or bomb interaction occurred.
observations.source_location: driver-second-sandbag.log final 10 lines; positions.tsv final 8 rows

observations.finding: The final pre-hold focus screenshot shows the player directly beside a steep rock slope, with a sandbag line farther to the right. The screenshot and accepted Y rise of 0.19 m make local terrain interference plausible; they do not establish a fixed collider or prove that 0.23 m was the maximum possible movement. The captured screenshot preceded the final accepted packet by about 1.15 seconds.
observations.source_location: focus-second.png (SHA-256 89cdf8b208ab1064cc014c916bf0cd1a95ce168cae38dffe3589aff17e65e89f), mtime 15:09:15.074 local; positions.tsv final packet at 15:09:16.223 local

observations.finding: Mission 1995 remained state 0, objective 1 active, objectives 2 and 3 complete; SQLite integrity was ok. The timer was reset only in the copied DB and was about five minutes from expiry when the driver stopped.

The supervisor wrote a normal stop command and observed its result, but immediately sent SIGTERM to the launcher before it had time to exit and write status.json. Launcher exit -15 and absent status.json are therefore caused by this supervisor cleanup race, not evidence of the earlier unexplained SIGTERM. The isolated processes were confirmed absent before DB restoration.
observations.source_location: supervisor-events.jsonl terminal_condition through children_terminal; stop command/result files; supervisor-state.json

assessment.finding: The waypoint 11 stop is both a strict-threshold event and a plausible local rock/slope interference, not a proven hard collision. The last packet's horizontal displacement was about 0.27 m and its target progress 0.23 m; a later hold or lateral heading was not tested. Original-client-derived navmesh queries from this area snap the start 1.4 m in Z and cannot resolve the exact player route. The corrected 8-second guard resolved the previously observed first-packet abort at waypoint 4, but the run did not reach the second sandbag.

tooling_followup.finding: Before another authorized isolated run, fix supervisor shutdown to wait for launcher exit and status.json after the stop result for a bounded grace period, then terminate only if still alive. At waypoint 11, capture the current view and test a small lateral/heading adjustment under fresh accepted-Move and terrain guards rather than treating the 0.23 m packet as a map defect.
